summary.text: You may use your MediSave for an approved dependant if they do not have enough MediSave. The withdrawal limit applies per patient.

details.heading: Withdrawal limits
details.body: The MediSave withdrawal limit applies per patient, regardless of how many people pay. If expenses remain after the limit is used, the remainder must be paid in cash.

steps.name: Check who qualifies
steps.text: You may use your MediSave if your family member is an approved dependant and does not have enough MediSave. Grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents; other approved dependants can be of any nationality.

items: Your spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings are approved dependants.
Grandparents and siblings must be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents; other approved dependants can be of any nationality.
You may use your MediSave if they do not have sufficient MediSave.

steps.name: Sign the authorisation form
steps.text: Approach the Medical Institution where your family member is receiving treatment and sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form. The hospital will submit the claim, and payment will go directly to the Medical Institution.

items: Approach the Medical Institution where your family member is receiving treatment.
Sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF).

about.text: The hospital submits the claim, and payment from your MediSave goes directly to the Medical Institution.

sources.page_title: Can I use my MediSave to pay for my family member’s outpatient treatment expenses?

quotes.text: If your approved dependants do not have sufficient MediSave for their outpatient treatment expenses, you may consider using your MediSave to pay for them.
Approved dependants refer to a member’s spouse, children, parents, grandparents and siblings.

Should you wish to use your MediSave for your approved dependants’ medical expenses, you may approach the Medical Institution (MI) where they are receiving treatment at to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF).
The hospital will then submit the claim to us and payment from your MediSave will be made directly to the MI.

While they can tap on your MediSave, the amount they can use is subject to the MediSave withdrawal limits, which is applied on a per patient basis regardless of the number of payers. If they still have outstanding medical expenses after utilising up to the MediSave withdrawal limit, they would have to pay the remainder in cash.
